subject: english-literature
title: Conventions and Twists
welcome_lead: When a story knows its genre, it can break the rules with style.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on genre conventions and subverting tropes.
final_note: You can now spot when a story follows and when it twists genre rules.

concepts.def: Hero who resists the call to adventure.

walkthroughs.body_html: A convention is expected (a fantasy quest). A trope is a familiar move (the chosen one). Both help readers feel at home.
Subverting a trope is twisting it. Shrek looks like a villain but acts like a hero — a fun subversion.
An anti-hero wins our attention without typical virtues — selfish, cynical, but compelling.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
